data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim hinges on a single large service achieving 'true independence' via formally verified isolation domains using different OS kernels and compiler toolchains. This conflates internal formal verification of isolation boundaries with statistical independence of failure modes. The problem asks for evidence that distinguishes truly independent failures from merely uncorrelated-appearing ones; even with diverse toolchains, two redundant subsystems of one large service share governance, threat-model, update cadence, and operational error-correlation. Formal isolation does not remove these shared-governance common causes, so SRC_001 overclaims by asserting that a single large service 'can achieve true independence' — at best it can reduce shared-dependency surface, not establish independence in the sense the problem demands.
